ip_top_stories.title: Brave Faces Two Publisher Lawsuits Over AI Use of News Content
ip_top_stories.summary: Brave Software is being sued by two groups of publishers over its AI-powered use of news content. The New York Times is among the plaintiffs in one action, with US newspapers and Canadian publishers filing separate suits — the latter against Anthropic — marking a significant escalation of legal pressure on AI browser and model developers over copyright in news content.

ip_top_stories.title: OpenAI Touts Briefs Backing Fair Use for AI Training
ip_top_stories.summary: OpenAI is highlighting amicus briefs filed in support of its fair use defence as the New York Times copyright case advances toward court. The briefs include submissions from the Irving Azoff Music Artists Coalition, Cate Blanchett, and the CCIA, while House Democrats have separately urged the court to reject the DOJ's position backing OpenAI's use of copyrighted journalism.

ip_top_stories.title: Wikimedia tells court: AI training is fair, copying articles isn't
ip_top_stories.summary: Wikimedia has filed in the OpenAI copyright case arguing that AI training on publicly available content can be fair use, but that ChatGPT's web retrieval feature — which reproduces article text directly — is not. The filing draws a legal distinction between training and inference-time copying that could have broad implications for how AI systems are assessed under copyright law.

ip_top_stories.title: Alphabet Shareholder Sues Executives Over AI Copyright Claims
ip_top_stories.summary: An Alphabet shareholder has filed a lawsuit against company executives over the company's exposure to AI copyright infringement claims, alleging that leadership failed to adequately manage legal risks arising from AI training practices. The case represents a novel escalation of AI copyright concerns into corporate governance and shareholder litigation.

ip_top_stories.title: Runway AI YouTube Scraping Class Action Survives Dismissal
ip_top_stories.summary: A class action lawsuit against Runway AI over the alleged scraping of YouTube videos to train its generative AI models has survived a motion to dismiss, allowing the case to proceed. The ruling is a notable development for AI training data litigation, keeping alive claims that Runway unlawfully used video content without authorisation.

ip_further_links.title: House Democrats Criticize Justice Dept. Support of OpenAI in Copyright Suit
ip_further_links.summary: Ranking Members Nadler, Raskin, and Johnson have written to the court urging it to reject the DOJ's arguments in favour of giving AI companies unlimited free use of copyrighted New York Times journalism for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: CCIA Files Joint Amicus Brief in AI Training Copyright Case
ip_further_links.summary: The Computer & Communications Industry Association has filed a joint amicus brief in a key AI training copyright case, arguing in favour of fair use for AI model training.

ip_further_links.title: Irving Azoff's Music Artists Coalition joins Cate Blanchett and CAA on AI licensing brief in New York Times' case against OpenAI
ip_further_links.summary: The Music Artists Coalition, alongside Cate Blanchett and the Creative Artists Agency, has filed an amicus brief in the NYT v. OpenAI case, pushing for licensing frameworks rather than unlimited fair use for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: AI giants promise publishers new way to block some scraping
ip_further_links.summary: Major AI companies have announced a new mechanism allowing publishers to block certain forms of AI scraping, though the scope and enforceability of the tool remain in question.

ip_further_links.title: Meta Platforms (META) Delays AI Scraping Policy After Publisher Backlash
ip_further_links.summary: Meta has delayed its AI data scraping policy following significant pushback from publishers, with the CMA also opening a Competition Act investigation into Meta's publisher terms.

ip_further_links.title: Big tech's national security case to gut copyright laws is a bluff, intelligence expert warns
ip_further_links.summary: An intelligence expert argues that AI companies' invocation of national security to justify weakening copyright protections for AI training is unfounded and should be rejected by policymakers.

ip_further_links.title: Disquiet grows in Albanese's back yard as Grayndler artists unite against 'insane' AI proposal
ip_further_links.summary: Artists in the Australian Prime Minister's own constituency of Grayndler are organising opposition to proposed AI copyright changes they describe as deeply harmful to creators.

ip_further_links.title: The AI Transparency Trap
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how AI transparency requirements in publishing and research may create new risks and unintended consequences for academic institutions and publishers.

ip_further_links.title: AI content retrieval 'eating away' at publishers | UK top 50: Reach sees biggest audience drop
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers report that AI-driven content retrieval is significantly eroding web traffic, with Reach experiencing the largest audience decline among UK top-50 publishers.

ip_further_links.title: Law firm's AI use doesn't warrant cutting legal fees, US appeals court rules
ip_further_links.summary: A US appeals court has ruled that a law firm's use of AI tools does not justify reducing its legal fees, providing early judicial guidance on the billing implications of AI in legal services.
